snapshot: 2026-11-10 morning (Europe/Rome), X API public metrics; views are impressions

demos.title: Saltline: browser FPS built from one-shot prompts
demos.author: Felix Rieseberg (@felixrieseberg, Anthropic)
demos.shows: Photoreal first-person shooter in a rainy cargo port. Author says every model, sound and texture was generated from scratch in about 8 hours for about $550 at API pricing (445M input tokens, mostly cached; 2.7M output).
demos.notes: Author works at Anthropic. Prompt shared in a reply: https://x.com/felixrieseberg/status/2119927483994907024

demos.title: Destructible voxel city in the browser
demos.author: Matt Shumer (@mattshumer_)
demos.shows: Voxel city where buildings, castles and bridges blow apart into debris and fire. The author says it came from a single prompt, and the post links a playable demo.

demos.title: Rainy Tokyo alley written in code
demos.author: Higgsfield (@higgsfield_ai)
demos.shows: Photoreal night alley with rain, neon reflections, a working street mirror and readable signs. The post says no video model was used.
demos.notes: Made with the Higgsfield MCP, and the clip carries their watermark.

demos.title: Cinematic dragon shot in Blender
demos.author: @dinosaurbtuq
demos.shows: Dragon breathing fire over a snowy peak. Author says Fable built the mesh, rig, fire sim and camera in Blender for $23.

demos.title: Mexico City market in code
demos.author: Higgsfield (@higgsfield_ai)
demos.shows: Market street scene with paper flags, a piñata and fruit stalls with prices, all rendered from code.

demos.title: Minecraft-style clone
demos.author: @intheworldofai
demos.shows: Voxel sandbox game with HDR shaders, volumetric clouds and reflective water. Author claims 24K lines of TypeScript and 859 tests from one prompt.

demos.title: 'The Edge': 4K Blender film from one prompt, live on stream
demos.author: Riley Brown (@rileybrown)
demos.shows: Fable wrote Blender code for a full room, animated 13 shots, rented 10 RunPod GPUs and rendered in 4K in 52 minutes for $5.75. Music and SFX were made with ElevenLabs.
demos.notes: Viewer @ZeroFoundry says they watched it live: https://x.com/ZeroFoundry/status/2119902437549191569 . Roberto Nickson reproduced a similar result: https://x.com/rpnickson/status/2119969928304357507 . The prompt refers to a Blender workflow used before.

demos.title: Fable 5.2 controls real robot arms
demos.author: Claude (@claudeai, official)
demos.shows: Two off-the-shelf robot arms driven through Claude Code solve a puzzle cube, unscrew a bottle cap, fit a gear and draw a robot.
demos.notes: On-screen labels say the footage is sped up and pauses are cut (for example '8× · pauses cut'). The 64.9% RoboDojo score is a separate simulation benchmark.

demos.title: 1 km² of Indiranagar from map data
demos.author: @anshu4321
demos.shows: 3D rebuild of a real Bangalore neighbourhood with a day-to-night shift and a metro line, made from map data and one prompt.

demos.title: Rocket launch to orbit simulation
demos.author: @Shannnu_18
demos.shows: Browser rocket simulation from the pad to a 210 km orbit. Author says it uses gravity, drag, thrust and guidance.

demos.title: Portals: 450+ code-drawn worlds
demos.author: Ethan Mollick (@emollick)
demos.shows: Endless fly-through of worlds linked by portals. Mollick says 25,000 agent runs built them, and the agents wrote themselves an 87,500-word rulebook.

demos.title: Rigged zombie hand in Blender
demos.author: Higgsfield (@higgsfield_ai)
demos.shows: Rigged hand model that crawls, backflips and gestures.

demos.title: Realtime honey simulation in WebGL
demos.author: Deedy Das (@deedydas)
demos.shows: Physics-based honey pour rendered in real time in the browser.

demos.title: Home voice-assistant hub designed by Fable
demos.author: Claude (@claudeai, official)
demos.shows: Device designed from a one-paragraph prompt: spec, components, four-layer PCB, enclosure and firmware. Diode manufactured the boards.
demos.notes: Humans assembled the devices with Claude guiding them.

demos.title: Fishslop game run
demos.author: Theo (@theo)
demos.shows: Underwater game built in 76 minutes for about $42. The author says it is 'not significantly better than Opus 5.5'.

demos.title: Code-painted 'photo' with ~700,000 strokes
demos.author: Jake Eaton (@jkeatn, Anthropic)
demos.shows: Still image of a parking garage painted stroke by stroke in a simulated paint engine. Author says no image model was used.
